tagline: Minify and clean SVG files to cut their size without losing quality
pageDescription: Optimize and minify SVG files with this free online SVG Optimizer powered by SVGO. Paste your markup or drop a file to strip comments, editor metadata, hidden layers and redundant attributes, collapse paths and shrink the file — often by 40–70% — while keeping the viewBox so it still scales perfectly. Everything runs locally in your browser, so your graphics are never uploaded and stay private. Ideal for faster-loading websites, smaller icon sets and cleaner inline SVG in your code.

instructions.title: How to optimize an SVG

steps.title: Add your SVG
steps.description: Paste the SVG markup into the box, or drop an .svg file exported from Figma, Illustrator or Inkscape.

steps.title: Choose pretty-print (optional)
steps.description: Leave it off for the smallest one-line output, or turn it on to keep the optimized SVG readable.

steps.title: Click Optimize SVG
steps.description: SVGO strips comments, metadata and editor cruft, collapses paths and removes redundant attributes in your browser.

steps.title: Check the savings and preview
steps.description: See the before/after size, the percentage saved, and a live preview to confirm the graphic still looks right.

steps.title: Copy or download
steps.description: Copy the optimized markup for inline use, or download the minified .svg file.

features: Powered by SVGO, the industry-standard optimizer
Strips comments, metadata and editor namespaces
Collapses paths and removes redundant attributes
Keeps the viewBox so SVGs still scale
Live preview of the optimized graphic
100% client-side — graphics never leave your browser
useCases: Shrink icons before adding them to a website
Clean up SVGs exported from Figma or Illustrator
Reduce inline SVG weight in React or Vue components
Optimize a whole icon set for faster page loads
Remove editor metadata before sharing a logo
Cut SVG sprite size for better performance
Prepare SVGs for an icon font or component library
proTips: Leave pretty-print off for production; turn it on for code review
The viewBox is kept on purpose so your SVG stays responsive
Re-optimizing an already-clean SVG is safe and just confirms the size
Exported design-tool SVGs usually shrink the most
Use the preview to catch any clipping before you ship it
Everything is local, so unreleased logos stay private
troubleshooting: Does not look like an SVG: make sure the markup contains an <svg> tag
Graphic looks broken: an external font or image reference may be missing — that's not in the SVG
Barely shrank: the SVG was already optimized, which is fine
Colors changed: a CSS variable or external style isn't included in the file
Preview is blank: the SVG may rely on scripts or external resources that don't render standalone
